text:
Evan Bouchard ended it 47 seconds into overtime, a snap shot with Leon Draisaitl assisting, and Edmonton took its third straight win. Bouchard was the tenth pick in 2018 out of the London Knights, and he finished with a goal and an assist in 26:30 of ice time. The Oilers needed all of it, because they spent most of the night chasing a game they had mostly not controlled.

Our numbers say PHI played the better game. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than just the count, favored the Flyers 3.02 to 2.58, and PHI had 66 shot attempts to EDM's 49. That works out to a 57% chance of winning if you replayed every shot, which is what we call deserved to win. PHI owned the first period, out-chancing EDM 1.12 to 0.43, and Tristan Jarry stopped Tyson Foerster on a 20% look there. Jarry saved about one goal more than his 32 shots against deserved, which is why he earned second star behind Zach Hyman, who scored twice. Hyman's second came on the power play, one of just 8 penalty minutes the Oilers took against the Flyers' 2.

Foerster did get one back, scoring on a 6% chance on the power play late in the second, and Travis Sanheim tied it at 2-2 in the third. EDM now has three straight wins, while PHI lost despite out-chancing its opponent.
